distinguishing_features: Physical damping/mitigation actuator rather than a monitoring or instability-prediction method.
Dedicated isolated coolant-loop reservoir/orifice/accumulator using fluid-column inertia as the damping mass.
Tuning to a spindle regenerative-chatter structural mode using spindle modal mass and target chatter frequency.
Solenoid diversion of coolant driven by spindle load current to engage the damper during cutting.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce regenerative spindle chatter and improve surface finish by suppressing the responsible structural vibration mode during cutting.
parsed.viable_reason: The proposal is not viable as written because k_eff = m_fluid/L is dimensionally invalid, the 450 Hz stiffness is miscomputed by about a factor of four, and a 1 L coolant reservoir cannot provide the required inertial mass/stiffness at that frequency.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Prior art 1 only infers oil-whirl onset from lubricant temperature and speed and provides no teaching or motivation to build a coolant-loop fluid-inertia damper for spindle chatter, so the distinguishing mechanism is not an obvious derivation from it.
